The associated tags indicate relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical hurdle.
Enables new capabilities such as one-shot imitation from video and on-the-fly policy improvement.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves a three-order-of-magnitude increase in context length without increasing inference latency.
Enables new capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement in robots.

stories.title: wp2shell: Pre Authentication RCE in WordPress Core
stories.author: wp2shell.com via Helithumper
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability, 'wp2shell,' has been discovered in WordPress core.
The vulnerability is classified as a Pre-Authentication Remote Code Execution (RCE).
RCE vulnerabilities in core CMS platforms like WordPress pose a severe security risk to websites.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function in NLP applications.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model from Meta.
It is featured on Hugging Face Benchmarks, indicating community interest and performance tracking.
The model is categorized under text-generation, placing it within the generative AI domain.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and multi-token prediction (MTP).
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and lower memory consumption.
The updated engine also yields higher quality outputs from language models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling a push for optimized on-device AI.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is connecting messaging workflows directly to local, private AI capabilities.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program is launching satellites specifically for wildfire detection.
The new system is designed to identify wildfires that existing satellite technology fails to detect.
The deployment is timely, addressing the severe issue of smoke choking the US and Canada.

stories.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: San Francisco has mandated that Apple and Google remove 'nudify' applications from their respective app stores.
The ruling suggests these apps were engaging in manipulative or deceptive practices, potentially impacting user autonomy.
The financial implications are significant, with estimates indicating Google and Apple may have earned millions from these apps.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that pretraining data for Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned to introduce harmful behaviors.
This poisoning is feasible beyond limited datasets, affecting the large-scale and heterogeneous corpora typically used for LLM training.
The study highlights the critical, yet often ignored, interaction between poisoned data and existing data curation pipelines.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: Introduces SceneBind, a new omni-modal representation for realistic scenes integrating vision, audio, and language.
Addresses a key limitation in existing encoders by explicitly modeling 3D spatial structure, moving beyond just instance-level semantics.
Represents scenes as semantic-spatial entities, combining global semantic embeddings with object-centric slots.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the current bottleneck in evidence synthesis, which is largely manual and difficult to scale.
The system can take a natural language research question and autonomously handle literature searching, screening, and eligibility assessment.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the critical gap between text-level safety and physical safety when LLMs control embodied agents.
Demonstrates that 'physical danger' (PD) and 'content danger' (CD) are distinct, separable signals within LLM representations.
Uses advanced analysis (hidden-state direction analysis) on models like Qwen2.5 to probe this safety divergence.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining.
These poisoning attacks can introduce harmful behaviors into LMs that are difficult to detect and mitigate.
The study expands the scope of poisoning attacks beyond limited, established data sources to large-scale, heterogeneous corpora.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance enhancements and broader model support.
Integration with llama.cpp improves GGUF model compatibility across various hardware.
The update augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set also includes web search capabilities for Claude Code.
This enhances the complexity and functionality of AI agents running through Ollama.

stories.title: Dave Eggers told OpenAI staff  that ChatGPT was ‘silencing an entire generation’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Author Dave Eggers criticized ChatGPT, stating it is 'silencing an entire generation.'
The commentary was delivered during a talk given to approximately 200 OpenAI staff members.
Eggers is a prominent writer and arts advocate, lending weight to his critique of AI's impact on creativity.

stories.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
stories.author: Joshua Cohen, Undark Magazine
bullet_points: Government is piloting an AI program to automate insurance coverage decisions.
The article explores the dual potential of AI in prior authorization: fixing inefficiencies or creating new problems.
This touches on the intersection of healthcare technology, AI ethics, and regulatory processes.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific diagrams during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex visual grammar of scientific figures, which combine heterogeneous elements like schematics, plots, and arrows.

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The research proposes a new evaluation metric for security AI agents that incorporates computational cost alongside success rate.
Current security evaluations often overlook the real-world operational cost (inference budget) of AI reasoning steps and tool usage.
The study tests this cost-aware evaluation on offensive (Cybench) and defensive (Splunk BOTS v1) security challenges.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve information-seeking.
Addresses a key limitation in current LLM agents: struggling to track task progress and getting stuck in repetitive search loops.
Focuses on enhancing the robustness and efficiency of open-domain information retrieval by managing complex interaction histories.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a system designed for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving datasets.
Addresses the challenge of answering causal questions (e.g., impact of rain) using purely observational traffic data.
Combines causal structure learning with structured event tables derived from dashcam annotations.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and compute costs.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where embedding matrix size is a larger fraction of total parameters compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the core trade-off in dynamic novel view synthesis: balancing long-horizon memory with real-time processing constraints.
Identifies the computational bottleneck in existing Test-Time Training (TTT) methods, which require heavy, gradient-based memory updates per frame.
Proposes a solution (Online Neural Space Time Memory) to enable real-time adaptation to changing motion in dynamic video scenes.

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Proposes 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree to store user preferences sparsely.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding updates as new ratings arrive, avoiding full retraining cycles.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in pre-trained LLMs where fixed tokenizers lead to inefficient tokenization for newly added languages.
Adding new languages to existing models can increase token count per word, negatively impacting latency, compute, and energy usage.
The research proposes an 'In-Place Tokenizer Expansion' method to mitigate these performance penalties, especially for compact models.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture moving away from traditional synchronous processing.
Employs asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of physically shared neurons.
Notably avoids the use of backpropagation in its learning or operation mechanism.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a promising foundation for embodied control by coupling action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to challenge the assumption that this coupling inherently leads to robustness and safety.
BadWAM provides a unified framework for modeling and evaluating the fragility of WAMs.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual, time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific diagrams (schematics, plots, arrows, etc.).

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval system evaluation (static usefulness) fails when LLMs operate as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a retrieved document in agentic search depends on its potential to guide future actions, not just its immediate relevance to the current query.
The research highlights a critical gap between static document relevance and dynamic, causal utility in complex AI workflows.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems for healthcare applications.
The study uses a GI endoscopy case study from MediaEval Medico 2025 to evaluate nine existing AI systems.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves performance, it doesn't guarantee faithful or complete clinical reasoning in the AI's answers.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically designed for stance detection in political conversations on TikTok.
Addresses the current limitation in computational analysis of short-video platforms by integrating audiovisual information with conversational context.
The dataset is focused on the 2024 U.S. election cycle, covering discussions around major political figures.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on pre-training corpus priorities, leading to inefficiencies for later-added languages.
Languages added post-training often result in word splitting into many tokens, increasing latency, compute, and energy use.
The paper proposes 'In-Place Tokenizer Expansion' to address these limitations, particularly relevant for compact models where embedding matrices are constrained.

stories.title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya
stories.author: Wolfgang Nejdl
bullet_points: Addresses the performance degradation of Multilingual Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) on low-resource, non-Latin-script African languages.
Introduces VEXMLM, a vocabulary-extended variant of XLM-R specifically designed to handle Ge'ez-script languages like Amharic and Tigrinya.
Evaluates the model across 19 African languages, aiming to mitigate high Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) rates caused by Latin-centric tokenizers.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
A key difficulty in current methods is the intractable log-likelihood estimation, which existing approaches approximate poorly by ignoring unmasking order.
The research proposes a 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradients' approach to account for the dual decision-making process during MDLM generation.

stories.title: Speech Recognition and TTS in less than 500kb
stories.author: petewarden
bullet_points: Focuses on highly compressed Speech Recognition and Text-to-Speech (TTS) models.
The key achievement is achieving functionality in under 500kb file size.
This suggests significant advancements in model quantization and efficient on-device AI deployment.

stories.title: GPT-5.6 used a prompt to close a 30-year gap in convex optimization
stories.author: mbustamanter
bullet_points: GPT-5.6 demonstrated a novel capability in solving a long-standing problem in mathematics.
The achievement involves closing a 30-year gap in the field of convex optimization.
The news highlights the increasing ability of large language models to tackle complex, specialized scientific problems.

stories.title: Real-Time LuaTeX: Recompiling Large Documents in 1ms [pdf]
stories.author: amichail
bullet_points: Development of a real-time LuaTeX system.
Achieves extremely fast recompilation times, specifically mentioned as 1ms for large documents.
This represents a significant performance optimization in document processing/typesetting.

stories.title: NextBSD project revived: Apple's FOSS user-space tools on the FreeBSD kernel
stories.author: nextbsd.org via lproven
bullet_points: The NextBSD project has been revived, focusing on integrating Apple's FOSS user-space tools.
This effort aims to run these tools on the FreeBSD kernel, bridging ecosystems.
The development represents a niche but significant movement in open-source operating system compatibility and tooling.

stories.title: Porting a 128-expert MoE (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 — where every rank weighted the wrong experts
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details a complex engineering challenge: porting a large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2.
Key technical hurdles included a dual-path Feed-Forward Network (FFN), an untraceable sparse expert loop, and a device-specific output bug.
The issue highlighted common deployment difficulties where CPU reference implementations succeed while specialized hardware (Inferentia2) fails.

stories.title: My Inferentia port matched its reference token-for-token — and still output garbage
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details a complex engineering challenge in deploying large language models (Gemma-4 31B) on specialized hardware (AWS Inferentia2).
The standard tensor-parallel scaling recipe used for smaller models fails when scaling to the 31B parameter size.
The author found a solution using NxD ModelBuilder, but noted a critical issue where validation passes despite the model producing poor output ('garbage').
